claim: Shinjuku Gyoen charges 500 JPY adult admission, opens 9:00–16:30 (last entry 16:00), closed Mondays, with seasonal extended hours during cherry blossom season.
quote: Admission is 500 JPY for adults, with discounted rates for students and free entry for children under age 15. Gates typically open from 9:00 a.m. to 4:30 p.m., with the last entry at around 4:00 p.m.

claim: Rikugien Garden is open 9:00–17:00 with 300 yen admission, extended to 20:30 during autumn illumination (late November) and cherry blossom season; built ~1700, recreates 88 poetic scenes.
quote: Regular Hours: 9:00 AM to 5:00 PM (entry until 4:30 PM) Evening Hours: Until 8:30 PM during autumn colors and cherry blossoms... Admission: 300 yen... 'reproduces in miniature 88 scenes from famous poems.'

claim: Hamarikyu Gardens open 9:00–17:00 daily (last entry 16:30) for 300 yen, feature a tidal seawater pond and the Nakajima teahouse where matcha costs 500 yen or 1,000 yen with wagashi.
quote: The garden is open 9 AM to 5 PM daily (closed Dec 29–Jan 1)... Tickets cost ¥300 for adults... Tea at Nakajima-no-ochaya is 500 yen, though a matcha set with nerikiri (traditional wagashi) or dorayaki is 1,000 yen each.

claim: Tokyo's three Grand Sumo tournaments at Ryogoku Kokugikan in 2026 are January 11–25 (Hatsu), May 10–24 (Natsu), and September 13–27 (Aki); tickets range 2,200–14,800 yen.
quote: January Tournament (Hatsu Basho): January 11–25, 2026; May Tournament (Natsu Basho): May 10–24, 2026; September Tournament (Aki Basho): September 13–27, 2026... Tickets range from ¥2,200 for same-day unreserved standing tickets to ¥14,800 for premium ringside masu box seats.

claim: Kabukiza offers hitomakumi (single-act) tickets letting tourists watch one scene at an affordable price without committing to a full 4-hour program; pricing varies by act and is announced per month.
quote: Single act performances are known as 'hitomakumi' in Japanese, and you can choose to watch particular scenes at an affordable price within a short time, making it an ideal way to enjoy kabuki for both novices and experts, as well as tourists who want to save some of their time for sightseeing.

claim: Tokyo National Museum opens 9:30–17:00 (until 20:00 Fri/Sat) for 1,000 yen adult admission, with the Gallery of Horyuji Treasures and the country's largest collection of Japanese art.
quote: Hours: 9:30 a.m. – 5:00 p.m. with extended hours until 8:00 p.m. on Friday, Saturday, and Sundays preceding holidays... Adults: 1,000 yen... It features the 'Gallery of Horyuji Treasures', displays Japanese archaeology, and showcases Asian art.

claim: Mori Art Museum in Roppongi Hills opens 10:00–22:00 (last entry 21:30, until 17:00 Tuesdays), focusing on contemporary art with admission around 2,000 yen depending on exhibition.
quote: Hours: 10:00-22:00 (Last Admission: 21:30) * 10:00-17:00 on Tuesdays (Last Admission: 16:30)... Admission depends on the current exhibition but adults can expect to pay around 2000 yen.

claim: Edo-Tokyo Open Air Architectural Museum in Koganei displays 30 relocated historic buildings on 7 hectares, open 9:30–17:30 (Apr–Sep) or 16:30 (Oct–Mar), 400 yen adult, closed Mondays; inspired Miyazaki's Spirited Away.
quote: The museum is open April-September from 9:30 AM to 5:30 PM and October-March from 9:30 AM to 4:30 PM... Admission costs 400 yen for adults... features historic buildings of high cultural value relocated to a seven-hectare site within Koganei Park, with a total of 30 buildings currently displayed.

claim: Hie Shrine in Akasaka and Nezu Shrine in Bunkyo are major historic shrines far less crowded than Meiji or Senso-ji; Gotokuji is the maneki-neko birthplace and Sengakuji holds the 47 Ronin graves.
quote: Hie Shrine - Located on the hilltops between Akasaka and Nagatacho, Hie Shrine is one of Tokyo's major shrines — but it isn't nearly as busy as Sensoji or Meiji Shrine... Gotokuji Temple - Widely known as the birthplace of the lucky beckoning cat, or maneki-neko.

claim: Nezu Shrine's Azalea Festival peaks April 10–20 each year with 3,000 bushes and a small festival admission fee, and the shrine's red torii corridor evokes a mini Fushimi Inari.
quote: The Nezu Azalea Shrine Festival typically reaches peak bloom between April 10 and April 20... During the festival, the garden is open daily from 9:30 AM to 5:30 PM with a small admission fee.

claim: Thermae-Yu in Shinjuku is Tokyo's most accessible onsen (open 22 hours, real Izu hot-spring water, tattoo-tolerant with stickers); Daikoku-yu in Oshiage is a renovated 1949 sento with a Mt Fuji mural at ~550 yen.
quote: Thermae-Yu is undoubtedly one of the best onsen experiences in Tokyo... Open 22 hours every day... Daikoku-yu... has been open since 1949 and holds one of the best views in Tokyo bathing... With an entrance fee of only around 550 yen.

claim: Happo-en garden runs walk-in tea ceremony Sat/Sun/Mon 11:00–15:00 for 1,100 yen per person, in a 500-year-old bonsai garden; Hamarikyu hosts the annual Tokyo Grand Tea Ceremony each October.
quote: Happo-en Tea Ceremony... available only on Saturday, Sunday and Monday with opening hours from 11am – 3pm (no reservations accepted) for 1,100 yen per person... The Tokyo Grand Tea Ceremony takes place at Hamarikyū Gardens on October 4-5 in 2026.

claim: The National Noh Theatre near Sendagaya Station stages year-round Noh/Kyogen on a stage of 400-year-old cypress with English audio guide and built-in seat-back subtitle screens.
quote: The National Noh Theatre, located just a five-minute walk from Sendagaya Station, is the perfect place to watch Nogaku... all seats are very comfortable with built-in screens to display the words of the performances that allow you to pick your language... made from the wood of 400-year-old cypress trees.

claim: Tokyo's 2026 cherry blossoms are forecast to open March 19 and reach full bloom around March 27–29, several days earlier than average due to a warm February.
quote: In 2026, the cherry blossom dates in Tokyo are expected to start on March 19th and peak on March 27th, which is a few days earlier than average... Tokyo cherry blossoms are forecast to peak between March 26 and March 29, 2026.
